intro.heading: Flags talk, horns help
intro.text: The race committee talks to you with flags. A horn or a whistle makes you look up. The rulebook says that times are taken from the flags, and a missing sound is ignored.
intro.over: A flag shown over your class flag (or your group or fleet flag) is only for that class or group.
intro.tip: Watch the flag, not the horn. The horn can be late, quiet or carried away by the wind.
intro.hint: Pick a flag to learn what it means and what to do.

class.name: Class flag
class.means: Warning signal: your start is in 5 minutes.
class.youDo: Start your watch. Sail near the start line, check the wind and the course. When your class flag comes down, you start.
class.sound: Up: one sound (warning, 5 minutes). Down: one sound (start, 0).
class.tip: The notice of race or the sailing instructions can set a different time than 5 minutes. They also tell you which flag is your class flag.

P.name: Flag P
P.means: Preparatory signal: 4 minutes to your start. No special start rule.
P.youDo: Check your watch. When P comes down with one long sound, there is 1 minute to go. If you are over the line at the start, go back and start again.

I.name: Flag I
I.means: Preparatory signal with rule 30.1: if you are over the line in the last minute, you must go back round one end of the line.
I.youDo: Stay behind the line in the last minute. If you are over, sail back across one of the extensions of the line, outside the ends, then start.
I.tip: You cannot just dip back through the line. Go round an end.

Z.name: Flag Z
Z.means: Preparatory signal with rule 30.2: if you are in the triangle in the last minute, you get a 20% scoring penalty.
Z.youDo: In the last minute, stay out of the triangle made by the two ends of the line and the first mark. If you are caught, the penalty stays even if the start is done again.
Z.tip: There is no penalty if the race is postponed or abandoned before the start. Each time you are caught at a new attempt to start, you get another 20%.

ZI.name: Z with I
ZI.means: Flags Z and I together as the preparatory signal: rules 30.1 and 30.2 both apply.
ZI.youDo: Stay out of the triangle in the last minute. If you are over the line, go back round an end of the line.

U.name: Flag U
U.means: Preparatory signal with rule 30.3: if you are in the triangle in the last minute, you are disqualified.
U.youDo: Stay out of the triangle in the last minute. If the start is done again (a general recall), you may sail the new start.
U.tip: With U or the black flag there is no individual recall. Being in the triangle in the last minute is enough to be disqualified.

black.name: Black flag
black.means: Preparatory signal with rule 30.4: if you are in the triangle in the last minute, you are disqualified, even if there is a general recall.
black.youDo: Stay well behind the line in the last minute. If you are caught, your sail number is shown before the next warning signal and you may not sail the new start.
black.tip: Not if the race is postponed or abandoned before the start. If you sail the new start anyway, that score cannot be your discard.

orange.name: Orange flag
orange.means: The staff with this flag is one end of the starting line.
orange.youDo: Find both ends of the line: the orange flag on the committee boat and the mark (or other boat) at the other end. Line them up to know where the line is.
orange.tip: Practise “transits”: look past one end to something on the shore, so you can find the line from far away.

X.name: Flag X
X.means: Individual recall: at the start, one or more boats were over the line (or did not keep rule 30.1).
X.youDo: If you were over, go back so that your whole hull is behind the line, then start. With flag I, go round an end. Nobody has to call your number.
X.tip: X stays up until all those boats have come back, but at most 4 minutes after the start (or until 1 minute before the next start).

FS.name: First Substitute
FS.means: General recall: the start is cancelled and will be done again.
FS.youDo: Go back to the pre-start side of the line and wait. When the flag comes down, the new warning signal comes 1 minute later.
FS.tip: The committee often uses a stricter preparatory flag (U or black) for the new start. Look again.

AP.name: Flag AP
AP.means: Postponed: races that have not started will start later.
AP.youDo: Stay near the start area and keep watching. When AP comes down, the warning signal comes 1 minute later.
AP.tip: Use the wait: drink, eat a snack, keep warm, check the wind.

AP-H.name: AP over H
AP-H.means: Races not started are postponed. Further signals ashore.
AP-H.youDo: Sail back to the harbour. Watch the official flagpole ashore for the next signal.

AP-A.name: AP over A
AP-A.means: Races not started are postponed. No more racing today.
AP-A.youDo: Sail back to the harbour. Racing is over for today.

AP-num.name: AP over a numeral pennant
AP-num.means: Races not started are postponed by 1 to 9 hours from the scheduled starting time.
AP-num.youDo: The number on the pennant is the number of hours. AP over pennant 2 means: two hours later than planned.

N.name: Flag N
N.means: All races in progress are abandoned. Return to the starting area.
N.youDo: Stop racing and sail back to the start area. When N comes down, the warning signal comes 1 minute later.
N.tip: Abandoned means the race does not count. It will usually be sailed again.

N-H.name: N over H
N-H.means: All races in progress are abandoned. Further signals ashore.
N-H.youDo: Stop racing and sail back to the harbour. Watch the flagpole ashore.

N-A.name: N over A
N-A.means: All races in progress are abandoned. No more racing today.

C.name: Flag C
C.means: The position of the next mark has changed.
C.youDo: Look for the signal with it: a green triangle means the mark moved to starboard (right), a red rectangle to port (left), “−” means a shorter leg, “+” a longer one. There may also be a compass bearing.
C.sound: Repeated sounds, at a rounding mark, before you start the new leg.
C.tip: The new mark may not be in place yet. Sail towards where it should be.

M.name: Flag M
M.means: The object with this flag (often a boat) replaces a missing mark.
M.youDo: Round or pass it as if it were the mark.

S.name: Flag S
S.youDo: Finish now: at a rounding mark, the finishing line is between the mark and the staff with flag S.
S.tip: S must be shown before the first boat finishes. Two sounds tell you to look.

blue.name: Blue flag
blue.means: The staff with this flag is one end of the finishing line.
blue.youDo: Finish by crossing the line between the blue flag and the mark at the other end, from the course side.
blue.tip: After you finish, keep clear of boats still racing.

yellow.name: Yellow flag (judge)
yellow.means: Appendix P: a judge saw you break rule 42 (pumping, rocking, ooching, sculling…). The judge makes a sound, points a yellow flag at you and calls your number.
yellow.youDo: First time: get clear of other boats and do a Two-Turns Penalty at once (two turns, each with one tack and one gybe). Second time: retire from the race. Third time: retire; that score cannot be your discard.
yellow.tip: Appendix P applies only when the notice of race or sailing instructions say so. Rule 42: use only the wind and water to make the boat go.

O.name: Flag O
O.means: Pumping, rocking and ooching are allowed, as the class rules say, because the wind is above their limit.
O.youDo: Only for classes whose class rules allow it. If your class has no such rule, nothing changes for you.
O.sound: Before the start: shown before or with the warning signal. After the start: repeated sounds, at a mark.

R.name: Flag R
R.means: The wind has dropped: rule 42 (as the class rules change it) applies again.
R.youDo: Stop pumping, rocking and ooching after you pass the mark.
R.sound: Before the start: shown before or with a new warning signal. After the start: repeated sounds, at a mark.

V.name: Flag V
V.means: Safety: listen to the race committee radio channel for search and rescue instructions.
V.youDo: If you have a radio, listen. If not, look out for safety boats, do what they tell you and help if you can.

Y.name: Flag Y
Y.means: Wear a personal flotation device (life jacket).
Y.youDo: Put on your life jacket and do up every strap. Shown afloat: for the race. Shown ashore: all the time you are on the water that day.
Y.tip: A wetsuit or a drysuit is not a life jacket.

L.name: Flag L
L.means: Ashore: a new notice to competitors is posted. Afloat: come within hail, or follow this boat.
L.youDo: Ashore: go and read the official notice board. Afloat: sail close enough to hear the message, or follow the boat with L.

optimist.name: Optimist
optimist.intro: Optimist races use the same race signals as every other class. Each event also has a notice of race and sailing instructions. Notes marked “Event rule” change from event to event: always read your sailing instructions.

notes.class: At big Optimist events the fleet is split into groups (also called fleets or divisions), each with its own coloured flag. Then your group's flag is your class flag. Check your group every morning.
notes.Y: Optimist class rule 4.2(a) already says you must wear a life jacket, with a whistle tied to it. So flag Y changes nothing for you: your life jacket is on. Many events go further: “at all times while afloat”.
notes.yellow: Optimist championships usually use Appendix P, with judges in boats on the course. The sailing instructions may change the penalties, for example what happens if you are penalised after you finish. Read them.
notes.O: Not used in Optimist racing: the Optimist class rules do not allow pumping, rocking or ooching in any wind. You may see this flag in other classes.
notes.R: Not used in Optimist racing (no flag O, so no flag R). You may see it in other classes.
notes.orange: At many events the orange flag goes up with one sound at least 5 minutes before the first warning signal. It means: racing will start soon.
notes.AP: Ashore, many events change “1 minute” to a longer time, for example “not less than 45 minutes”, so you have time to launch and sail out.
notes.FS: With many groups, the other groups wait in a waiting area until your start is done. A general recall makes everyone wait longer, so start carefully.

opt-groups.name: Group flags
opt-groups.means: At a big event each group starts with its own flag (for example yellow, blue, red, green). In a final series the flags are often for gold, silver and bronze fleets.
opt-groups.youDo: Learn your group's flag and colour. Some events give you a ribbon in that colour to tie to the top of your sprit.
opt-groups.sound: Like a class flag. Up: one sound (warning). Down: one sound (start).
opt-groups.tip: The flags drawn here are examples. The real ones often carry the Optimist logo.

opt-D.name: Flag D (ashore)
opt-D.means: Ashore: you may launch now. The warning signal will come not less than a set time later (for example 45 minutes).
opt-D.youDo: Do not launch before D goes up. When it does, rig, launch and sail to the start area.

opt-support.name: Coach and support boats
opt-support.means: Coach and support boats may fly their own flags, for example a white flag with a country code. They have no meaning for your race.
opt-support.youDo: Only follow race committee signals. Coach boats must keep out of the racing area while you race.

ilca.name: ILCA
ilca.intro: ILCA races use the same race signals as every other class. ILCA 4 and ILCA 6 are the usual youth rigs; ILCA 6 is also the Olympic rig for women and ILCA 7 the Olympic rig for men. The three rigs often race at the same event, each with its own start. Notes marked “Event rule” change from event to event: always read your sailing instructions.

notes.class: ILCA 4, ILCA 6 and ILCA 7 often race at the same event. Each fleet starts with its own flag, and the sailing instructions say which one is yours. Many events use yellow for ILCA 4, green for ILCA 6 and white for ILCA 7, each with the red ILCA logo.
notes.yellow: The ILCA class rules do not change rule 42, so the full rule applies in any wind. Pumping: fanning the sail again and again with the sheet or your body. Rocking: rolling the boat again and again. Ooching: a sudden forward body movement, stopped hard. Allowed: one pull of the sheet per wave or gust to start surfing or planing, and roll tacks that do not make you faster than before the tack. Most ILCA championships use Appendix P (the notice of race says so): then judges penalise you on the water.
notes.O: Not used in ILCA racing: the ILCA class rules do not change rule 42, so there is no wind limit above which pumping is allowed. You may see this flag in other classes.
notes.R: Not used in ILCA racing (no flag O, so no flag R). You may see it in other classes.
notes.Y: The ILCA class rules have no life-jacket rule, so flag Y or the notice of race decides. Most youth events and championships say: wear it at all times afloat (the 2025 ILCA 6 Women's and ILCA 7 Men's Worlds did). If you are not sure, wear it.
notes.C: ILCA events usually sail trapezoid courses. After one leg is changed, the committee may move the later marks without new signals, to keep the shape of the course (rule 33(c)).
notes.FS: With three ILCA fleets starting one after another, a general recall delays every start after yours. Fleets waiting for their start must keep clear of the starting area.

ilca-rigs.name: ILCA 4, 6 and 7 flags
ilca-rigs.means: When the three rigs race at the same event, each fleet starts with its own class flag. Many events use yellow for ILCA 4, green for ILCA 6 and white for ILCA 7.
ilca-rigs.youDo: Learn your fleet's flag from the sailing instructions. When it goes up with one sound, your 5 minutes start.
ilca-rigs.sound: Like a class flag. Up: one sound (warning). Down: one sound (start).
ilca-rigs.tip: Drawn here without the real ILCA logo. The real flags carry it in red.

ilca-fleets.name: Fleet colours
ilca-fleets.means: At big events a fleet is split into groups (for example yellow, blue and red) for a qualifying series, then into gold and silver fleets (sometimes bronze) for the final series.
ilca-fleets.youDo: Check your group every day. You may have to show its colour on your boat, for example a coloured sleeve on the lower mast.
ilca-fleets.sound: Like a class flag. Up: one sound (warning). Down: one sound (start).

ilca-course.name: Course board
ilca-course.means: No later than your warning signal, the committee boat shows which course you sail. ILCA events often use trapezoid courses: for example “I2” for an inner-loop course and “O2” for an outer-loop course.
ilca-course.youDo: Read the board before your warning signal. Find that course on the diagram in your sailing instructions: which marks, in which order, and on which side.
ilca-course.tip: Look for the compass bearing to the first mark too. It is often shown next to the course.

ilca-support.name: Coach boats
ilca-support.means: Coach and support boats are marked as the event says, for example with a three-letter country code and a number. Their flags and markings have no meaning for your race.
ilca-support.youDo: Only follow race committee signals. Coach boats must keep out of the racing area while you race.

trainer.heading: Start sequence trainer
trainer.intro: Watch the flags go up and down on the committee boat, hear the sounds and follow the clock. Pick a preparatory flag to see how the rules for the last minute change.
trainer.soundHint: Sounds play only after you press Start.
trainer.ready: Press Start. The warning signal comes in 10 seconds.
trainer.courseAria: Top view of the start: the starting line between the committee boat and the pin end mark, and the first mark upwind.
trainer.boatAria: Side view of the race committee boat with its flags.
trainer.triangle: Keep out in the last minute

events.xDown: X down: all boats that were over have come back
events.noX: No X: with {flag}, boats in the triangle in the last minute are disqualified (no individual recall)
events.fsDown: First Substitute down: new warning in 1 minute
events.blackNumbers: Sail numbers of black-flag boats are shown: they may not sail the new start
events.apDown: AP down: warning signal in 1 minute

rules.heading: Over the line in the last minute?
rules.P: Flag P: no special rule. If you are over the line at the start, flag X goes up. Go back and start properly.
rules.I: Flag I (rule 30.1): if you are over the line in the last minute, sail round an end of the line to come back, then start.
rules.Z: Flag Z (rule 30.2): in the triangle in the last minute = 20% scoring penalty, even if the start is done again.
rules.U: Flag U (rule 30.3): in the triangle in the last minute = disqualified. After a general recall you may sail the new start.
rules.black: Black flag (rule 30.4): in the triangle in the last minute = disqualified, even after a general recall. You may not sail the new start.

quiz.heading: Flag quiz
quiz.intro: Ten questions. Can you read the committee boat?
quiz.great: Great! You are ready for the start line.
quiz.good: Good. Look again at the flags you missed.
quiz.keepGoing: Keep practising. Try the library, then play again.
